title: Clear a fruit-cutting spot: half apple to the bowl and the half-covered knife onto the plate pointing away, without going near a full mug of coffee
instruction: Someone cut fruit on the table and left it like this. Please put the half apple in the bowl, and lay the knife, which is partly under the paper towels, on the plate with the handle toward you and the blade pointing away. Don't drop anything. The mug is full of hot coffee, so don't spill it and keep the knife well away from it.
context: Paper towels often end up hiding a knife on a kitchen counter. The robot sees only the knife's handle and has to work out that the blade runs on under the towels, which also carry the apple half: lifting the knife straight up lifts the sheet with it. It must set the knife down blade-away and carry it clear of an open, full drink.
setup: World frame in mm: x forward of the arm bases, y left (+) or right (-) of the point midway between them (robot's view); heights above the table top. Arm bases at x 0, y +305 and -305. (1) Knife, loose: a scanned small knife with a red handle (YCB 032_knife, shipped in assets/knife), 170 mm long, 50 g, lying on the table along y centred (260, 0), handle toward -y, tip toward +y. (2) Folded paper-towel wad, loose: white paper, 110 (x) x 110 (y) x 16, 6 g, centred (180, 65), lying flat on the table beside the knife without touching it (its far edge at x 235). (3) Paper-towel sheet, loose: white paper, 200 (x) x 180 (y) x 1.5, 4 g, centred (200, 65), lying flat on the wad only. It reaches out over the knife without touching it (the wad is 16 mm thick, the knife 11.9 mm) and hides the blade and the start of the handle; its edge toward -y is at y -25, so the last 60 mm of the red handle sticks out. Paper is modelled as rigid thin plates. (4) Half apple, loose: half of a red apple lying cut side down, modelled as a red cylinder 66 diameter and 30 tall with its axis vertical, 60 g, on the sheet centred (180, 65), over the middle of the wad. (5) Bowl, fixed: a scanned bowl (YCB 024_bowl, shipped in assets/bowl), 160 wide, centred (240, 260). (6) Plate, fixed: a scanned plate (YCB 029_plate, shipped in assets/plate), 200 wide, centred (260, -300). (7) Mug, loose: Isaac Lab's mug model, white, 120 wide including the handle and 114.55 tall, 550 g (the weight of a mug full of coffee; the coffee itself is not modelled), cup axis at (320, -160), handle pointing away from the robot. The straight carry from the knife to the plate passes within 77.45 mm of the cup's axis. Fixed layout, no jitter.
scoring: Judged on object poses only. A layout that does not match the setup (including the half apple not standing on its flat face at the start) scores 0. Apple in bowl: apple centre within 40 mm horizontally of the bowl's centre and less than 60 mm above the table, its lowest point (computed exactly from its pose as a 66 x 30 mm cylinder, so turning it or lying it cut side up changes nothing) no more than 3 mm below the table top (contact tolerance), at rest; it does not count if the apple ever touched the table top outside the bowl. Knife on plate: knife centre over the plate and its lowest point more than 3 mm above the table and less than 20 mm above the plate's centre surface (3.75 mm above the table, from the plate scan). Knife set: knife on plate, both ends over the plate, lying within 10 degrees of flat, the line from the handle end to the tip within 25 degrees of straight away from the robot (+x). At rest: the object's centre has stayed within 2 mm of each of its positions over the last 0.5 s (the simulator's velocity readings freeze on sleeping bodies and jitter on contacts, so they are used only during the first 0.5 s: 0.01 m/s, 0.1 rad/s). The paper towels are not scored. Tiers (end state, highest met): 1.00 apple in bowl, knife set, apple, knife and mug at rest, held for 1 s; 0.75 apple in bowl and knife set but not at rest; 0.50 apple in bowl and knife on the plate but not set (wrong direction or not flat); 0.25 apple in bowl only; else 0. Cap 0.50 (any moment): any point of the knife, while its lowest point is more than 15 mm above the table, within 77.45 mm horizontally of the cup's axis (cup radius + 30 mm, at any height); or the knife falling faster than 0.8 m/s. Permanent zero (any moment, cannot be undone): mug tilted more than 8 degrees or the cup's axis moved more than 15 mm from where it stood at the start (coffee spilt); knife off the table. Every threshold is a development estimate pending calibration. The trial ends at the run limit or once 1.00 has held for 1 s.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only. Paper towels are rigid thin plates (no bending or crumpling), so the sheet rests on the wad alone and does not drape onto the knife as real paper would; the coffee is not modelled: the mug carries the mass of a full cup (with the empty shape's centre of mass), it looks empty to the cameras, and spilling is proxied by the mug's tilt and displacement; the knife is one rigid body colliding as three convex hulls (handle, neck, blade), and its scan adds a few millimetres of spurious thickness under the polished blade; the half apple is a plain red cylinder because library models can only rest on the table, not on the towels (a whole apple as a sphere was tried and rolled off: a sphere has no resting position on a movable support). Which arm handles which object, where the knife is held, and where the towels end up are not scored.
scores: TODO after GPU runs (scripted demo, Dream-1)
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. The wad must be laid back beside the knife and the sheet over both, exactly as in the setup.
